root.name: Blackmar-Diemer Gambit: Netherlands Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. e4 dxe4 3. Nc3 f5

overview: After 1.d4 d5 2.e4 dxe4 3.Nc3 Black defends the extra pawn with ...f5 instead of ...Nf6. White usually plays 4.g4, 4.Bg5 or 4.f3 to open lines against a king loosened by the f-pawn advance. Play is open and tactical, with White chasing a lead in development and Black trying to consolidate the pawn.

white_ideas.idea: Hit the weakened e8-h5 diagonal and the kingside with Bg5, Qh5+ or g4 ideas
Develop quickly with f3 or Bc4 and Nge2, recovering the pawn or attacking

black_ideas.idea: Keep the e4 pawn with ...f5 and ...Nf6
Trade pieces and use the extra pawn in the endgame

typical_structures.structure: Open centre after the e-pawn exchange, Black pawns on e6 and f5 against an open f-file

character.notes: Open tactical gambit play with a loosened Black king.

gambit.notes: White offered the e-pawn and Black has not given it back by force.

soundness.notes: Parent BDG is judged insufficient for White by engines; ...f5 is a risky reply that loosens Black, so the verdict is close to level and uncertain.

structure.notes: Open: the e-pawn is gone and White plays for open files and diagonals.

approach.notes: A rare gambit line that strong players seldom choose.

level.notes: Tactical lines to know, and a dubious gambit is not a first-repertoire pick.

sublines_that_differ.name: Pohmlann with 4.g4
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. e4 dxe4 3. Nc3 f5 4. g4
sublines_that_differ.how: A sharper pawn break that opens the kingside at once.

character.reason: Open gambit lines with a loosened king and forcing play.

gambit.reason: White offers the e-pawn and Black can keep it.

soundness.reason: Engines call BDG compensation insufficient, though the line is playable below master level.

structure.reason: The e-file opens straight away and pieces fight on open lines.

approach.reason: Strong players hardly ever play the BDG or this reply.

level.reason: Dubious lines are never beginner and the tactics need learning.

plans.reason: White develops fast against the king.
